drivers.name: Allen & Heath Avantis Digital Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Allen & Heath Avantis digital mixing consoles via MIDI over TCP/IP on port 51325. Mute / fader / send level / assign control across all 96 inputs, 54 mono and 27 stereo groups, 54 mono and 27 stereo aux outs, 54 mono and 27 stereo matrix outs, 12 mono and 12 stereo FX sends, 12 FX returns, 3 mains, 16 DCAs, 8 mute groups, plus 8 stereo UFX sends and returns. Scene recall (1-500), channel name and colour set, MIDI Machine Control transport, UFX global key and scale, and bidirectional state from console-side change echoes.

help.overview: Controls an Allen & Heath Avantis digital mixing console over the network using MIDI over TCP/IP. Full mute, fader, send-level and assign control plus scene recall, MIDI Machine Control, channel name and colour, and UFX global key and scale. Console-side moves push back into OpenAVC state so faders and mute LEDs on a touch panel stay in sync.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the console is running firmware V2.0 or later. TCP/IP control is unavailable on earlier firmware.
2. Connect the Avantis to the same network as the OpenAVC server.
3. On the Avantis, go to Utility / Network and note the IP address.
4. Go to Utility / Control / MIDI and note the base MIDI channel (default 12). The console reserves the next four channels above the base for output buses, so the base cannot exceed 12.
5. Enter the IP address and matching base MIDI channel in the device config. The default port (51325) is correct.
6. The driver listens for console-side push automatically; no further setup is required.

compatible_models.notes: Same MIDI command surface across the Avantis family. Requires console firmware V2.0 or later for TCP/IP control.

drivers.name: Allen & Heath dLive Digital Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Allen & Heath dLive digital mixing systems (MixRack + Surface) via MIDI over TCP/IP on port 51325. Mute / fader / send level / send assign / channel assign across 128 inputs, 62 mono and 31 stereo groups, 62 mono and 31 stereo aux outs, 62 mono and 31 stereo matrix outs, 16 mono and 16 stereo FX sends, 16 FX returns, 6 mains, 24 DCAs, 8 mute groups, 8 stereo UFX sends, 8 stereo UFX returns. Adds dLive-specific surface: 128 socket preamps (gain via Pitchbend, Pad, 48V), per-channel HPF, Cue List Recall (Surface, 1-2000), Scene Recall (MixRack, 1-500), channel name and colour set, MMC transport, UFX global key and scale, plus bidirectional state from console-side echoes.

help.overview: Controls an Allen & Heath dLive digital mixing system over the network using MIDI over TCP/IP. Full mute, fader, send-level, send-assign, channel-assign, preamp (gain / pad / 48V), HPF, scene / cue recall, MMC and UFX global key / scale. Console-side moves push back into OpenAVC state so faders and mute LEDs on a touch panel stay in sync.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the dLive system is running firmware V2.0 or later. TCP/IP control is unavailable on earlier firmware.
2. Connect the MixRack (or Surface, if controlling the Surface directly) to the same network as the OpenAVC server.
3. On the dLive, go to Utility / Network and note the IP address.
4. Go to Utility / Control / MIDI and note the base MIDI channel. The console reserves the next four channels above the base for output buses.
5. Enter the IP address and matching base MIDI channel in the device config. Use port 51325 for MixRack, 51328 for Surface.
6. The driver listens for console-side push automatically; no further setup is required.

compatible_models.notes: Same MIDI command surface across the dLive S- and C-class Surfaces and DM-series MixRacks. Requires firmware V2.0 or later for TCP/IP control. Plain-TCP (port 51325) only in v1.0.0; TLS+UserProfile auth on port 51327 is a future extension.

drivers.name: Allen & Heath SQ Digital Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Allen & Heath SQ-5, SQ-6 and SQ-7 digital mixing consoles via MIDI over TCP/IP on port 51325. Full mute / level / pan / assignment control across all 48 inputs, 12 groups, 12 aux outs, 3 matrix outs, 4 FX sends, 8 FX returns, 8 DCAs, and 8 mute groups. Scene recall (1-300), 1 dB increment/decrement, SoftKey triggers, and bidirectional state — console-side moves push back into OpenAVC state.

help.overview: Controls an Allen & Heath SQ digital mixing console over the network using MIDI over TCP/IP. Full mute, level, pan and assignment control plus scene recall and SoftKey triggers. Console-side moves push back into OpenAVC state so faders and mute LEDs on a touch panel stay in sync.
help.setup:
1. Connect the SQ to the same network as the OpenAVC server.
2. On the SQ, go to Utility → General → Network and note the IP address.
3. Go to Utility → General → MIDI and note the MIDI Channel.
4. Enter the IP address and matching MIDI channel in the device config. The default port (51325) is correct.
5. The driver subscribes to console-side updates automatically; no further setup is required.

compatible_models.notes: Same MIDI command set across all three. SQ-5 has 8 SoftKeys (triggers 9-16 are no-ops). SoftKeys are addressed by integer 1-16.

drivers.name: AtlasIED Atmosphere
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls AtlasIED Atmosphere AZM4 and AZM8 audio processing and control systems over the third-party JSON-RPC protocol on TCP port 5321. Covers source / zone / mix / group gain and mute, zone source select, group combine, message and routine and scene playback, GPO state, and today's bell schedule. Subscribes for state updates on connect.

help.overview:
AtlasIED Atmosphere is a configurable audio DSP / mixer / paging system widely deployed in restaurants, retail, fitness, and house-of-worship installs. This driver speaks the third-party JSON-RPC protocol on TCP port 5321. It subscribes to entity state on connect, so updates push live as users change settings on the front panel or in the web UI.

Parameter names are assigned during device configuration (via the Atmosphere web UI). The driver addresses entities by zero-based index — Source 0, Zone 0, etc. Use the Atmosphere web UI's Settings → Third Party Control → Message Table to map names to indices.
help.setup:
1. In the Atmosphere web UI, go to Settings → Third Party Control → General and toggle 'Enable' on for the third-party control API.
2. Confirm the Atmosphere has a static IP (or DHCP reservation).
3. In OpenAVC, enter the IP. Port 5321 is fixed.
4. Set the entity counts (zones, sources, mixes, groups) to match the device configuration. Counts default to AZM8 sizing; over-sizing is harmless but bigger than needed clutters the state list.
5. After connecting, confirm the source / zone / mix / group names from the Atmosphere config show up in the device state.

compatible_models.notes: AZM4 / AZM8 are the standalone DSPs; AZMP4 / AZMP8 add internal amplification but share the same third-party control surface.

drivers.name: Atlona AT-OME-MS Series Matrix Switcher
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-OME-MS family of 4K/UHD matrix presentation switchers (MS42 / MS42-HDBT / MS52 / MS52W / MS52W-EU) over Telnet on TCP port 23. Routes any of five inputs (USB-C / DisplayPort / HDMI / HDMI / BYOD) to two outputs (HDBaseT and HDMI), with audio volume / mute (HDMI and analog independently), CEC display control, USB host switching, and per-input signal detection. Use this driver for the Display:Matrix:Set protocol family; the older PS62 with its xNAVxM syntax is covered by atlona_ome_ps62.

help.overview: AT-OME-MS matrices route HDMI / DisplayPort / USB-C sources to a HDBaseT extender output and a local HDMI output. Audio is independent of video routing — the HDMI and analog outputs each have their own mute and a shared system volume in dB. Display power can be controlled over CEC. USB host follow modes let a connected control host follow the active video source.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation).
2. If Telnet Login Mode is ON in the matrix's web UI (System tab), enter the same Username and Password used for the web GUI in this driver's config. Leave both blank if Telnet Login Mode is OFF.
3. Atlona requires at least 500 ms between commands; the driver enforces that automatically.
4. Use Set Matrix Mode to switch between single-input (both outputs follow Display:Input:Set) and matrix mode (per-output routing via Display:Matrix:Set).

compatible_models.notes: All MS-series presentation matrices share the dotted Display:Matrix:Set / Audio:Volume:Set command vocabulary. MS42 (4x2) inputs 0-3, MS52/MS52W (5x2) inputs 0-4. The MS52W adds a 4 = BYOD wireless-link input. Outputs are always 0=HDBaseT, 1=HDMI. The driver advertises the 0-4 input range; the device rejects anything it doesn't have.

drivers.name: Atlona AT-OME-PS62 Matrix Switcher
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-OME-PS62 6x2 4K/UHD matrix presentation switcher over Telnet on port 23. Routes any of six inputs (HDMI / USB-C / HDBaseT) to two outputs (HDBaseT and HDMI). Independent four-zone audio with per-zone volume and mute, analog audio source routing, USB host switching, front-panel lock, and identify (POWER LED blink).

help.overview: The PS62 routes six HDMI / USB-C / HDBaseT sources to a HDBaseT and a HDMI output. Audio is independent: each of the two video outputs and two analog audio outputs has its own volume and mute. Analog audio can follow the HDBaseT or HDMI feed, or pull from one of three auxiliary inputs.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation). 2. If Telnet Login Mode is ON in the matrix's web UI, enter the same
   Username / Password used for the web GUI in this driver's config.
   Leave both blank if Telnet Login Mode is OFF.
3. Atlona requires a 500 ms minimum delay between commands; the driver
   is pre-configured for this.

compatible_models.notes: 6x2 4K/UHD matrix presentation switcher with USB hub. The MS42 / MS52 / MS52W family in the OME line uses a completely different command syntax (Display:Matrix:Set...) and is covered by a separate driver.

drivers.name: Atlona AT-UHD-PRO3 Matrix
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Atlona AT-UHD-PRO3 series of HDBaseT matrix switchers (PRO3-44M / 66M / 88M / 1616M) via Telnet on port 23. Supports source routing (per output, all outputs, multi-output), per-output volume and mute, power, presets (save / recall / clear), front-panel lock, and identify. State is mirrored for outputs 1-10 (covers 88M fully; 1616M outputs 11-18 are routable but not state-mirrored).

help.overview: Atlona PRO3 matrices route HDMI sources to HDBaseT extender outputs over a Cat5e/6 link to remote receivers. Use the Route command to send a source to a specific output, the Route to All command to send one source everywhere, and per-output volume / mute for HDBaseT zone audio. Save up to 50 routing presets.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the matrix via its web UI (or DHCP reservation). 2. If IPLogin is enabled (factory default), enter the Username and
   Password configured on the matrix in this driver's config — the
   driver handles the "Login:" / "Password:" handshake automatically.
   Leave both blank if you've turned IPLogin off (per KB01392).
3. Atlona requires a 500 ms minimum delay between commands; the
   driver sends commands at that rate by default.
4. To activate a routing preset from a macro: configure the routing
   you want via individual Route commands, then send the Save Preset
   command with a preset number. Recall later with Recall Preset.

compatible_models.notes: AT-UHD-PRO3 series HDMI-to-HDBaseT matrix switchers. Output ranges vary by model (44M: 1-4, 66M: 1-6, 88M: 1-7+9 HDBaseT plus 8/10 HDMI mirrors, 1616M: 1-16+ mirrors). Driver state mirrors outputs 1-10. Larger 1616M outputs (11-18) accept routing commands but don't update state. Send a "Mreset" or "All#" to recover from surprising routing if a manual front-panel change happens.

drivers.name: Atlona OmniStream
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Atlona OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the Telnet CLI (port 23). Supports source routing, audio mute/volume, video enable, HDCP, analog speaker power, and CEC/RS-232 display triggers. Runtime control surface only — install-time setup is configured in the device's web UI.

help.overview: Atlona OmniStream is an AV-over-IP encoder/decoder system. Encoders take HDMI sources and produce network streams; decoders pick a stream and output HDMI to a display. Routing happens by setting which IP stream each decoder receives (the VideoInput command).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the OmniStream unit via its web UI. 2. If Telnet login authentication (IPLogin) is enabled on the device,
   enter the unit's Username and Password in this driver's config —
   the driver will handle the "Login:" / "Password:" handshake. Leave
   both blank if IPLogin is disabled.
3. Configure encoder sessions (multicast addresses, video format)
   and decoder IP inputs in the web UI before driver use.
4. Connect this driver to port 23. The HDMI output index ranges
   1..2 on most decoders; the session index ranges 1..6.
5. Volume range is 0..15 (Atlona's native scale). 6. To route a source: send the "Set Video Input" command with the
   output number and the IP input name (e.g. "ip_input3") configured
   on the decoder's web UI.

compatible_models.notes: All OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate models on firmware 2.0+. Some audio commands (mute, volume, AudioInput, AnalogPower, DisplayBtn, VolumeBtn, InputBtn) are Pro-only and silently no-op on R-Type units.

drivers.name: Dante DDM / Director
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Dante audio routing via the Audinate Managed API. Requires Dante Domain Manager or Dante Director Professional. Discover devices, route/unroute audio channels, monitor subscriptions.

help.overview:
This driver connects to a Dante Domain Manager (DDM) or Dante Director Professional instance to control audio routing across all Dante devices on the network. It does NOT connect to individual Dante devices — the DDM/Director acts as the central management point.

You can route any transmit (Tx) channel to any receive (Rx) channel, clear routes, and monitor subscription status.
help.setup:
1. You need Dante Domain Manager (on-premise) or Dante Director Professional (cloud) — the Standard tier does not include API access.
2. Generate an API key in the DDM/Director web UI.
3. Enter the DDM/Director URL (e.g., https://ddm.local or the Director cloud URL).
4. Enter the API key.
5. Enter the Dante domain name to manage (shown in DDM/Director).
6. Use the 'refresh' command to discover devices and channels.

drivers.name: Audio-Technica ATDM-0604
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-0604 Digital SmartMixer via TCP. Supports input/output level and mute control, preset recall, and SmartMix configuration.

help.overview: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-0604 Digital SmartMixer. The ATDM-0604 is a 6-input, 4-output automatic mixer designed for conference and installed sound applications.
help.setup: 1. Connect the ATDM-0604 to the network. 2. The default control port is 17300. 3. Configure the device's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 4. Input channels: 1-6 (mic/line), ST (stereo). 5. Output channels: 1-4, ST (stereo).

drivers.name: Audio-Technica ATDM-1012
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-1012 and ATDM-1012DAN Digital SmartMixers via TCP. Supports input/output level and mute control, bus assign, SmartMix configuration, operator faders, and preset recall.

help.overview: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-1012 / ATDM-1012DAN Digital SmartMixers. The ATDM-1012 is a 10-input, 8-output automatic mixer with 12 mix buses, designed for conference rooms, courtrooms, and council chambers. The DAN variant adds Dante audio networking.
help.setup: 1. Connect the ATDM-1012 to the network. 2. The default control port is 17300. 3. Configure the device's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 4. Input channels: 1-10 (mic/line), ST1, ST2, Sub 1-8. 5. Output channels: 1-8, ST1, ST2. 6. The ATDM-1012DAN uses the same protocol with added Dante settings.

drivers.name: AVer Pro-AV PTZ Camera (PTZ310/330)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: AVer Pro-AV PTZ310 / PTZ330 family. Combines VISCA-over-IP (UDP 52381) for power, PTZ motion, and position inquiries with AVer's HTTP CGI (port 80, /storks) for image quality (shutter, iris, gain, white balance, color temperature, saturation, contrast, sharpness), AI features (SmartShoot, SmartFraming), bulk status query, RTMP streaming, mirror/flip, and reboot. For other AVer models without a documented HTTP CGI guide, prefer the generic 'visca_ip' driver.

help.overview: AVer PTZ310 / PTZ330 broadcast PTZ cameras. Common in houses of worship, lecture capture, courtroom recording, and corporate AV. Image quality (gain, iris, shutter, white balance, color temperature, sharpness, mirror/flip) and AVer's SmartShoot / SmartFraming AI features are controlled over HTTP. Power, pan/tilt/zoom motion, and position inquiries use VISCA-over-IP.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and place it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. The driver opens TWO connections: VISCA-over-IP on UDP 52381 and HTTP on TCP 80. Both must be reachable.
3. Most CGI commands require no authentication. The Reboot and Factory Reset commands require Basic auth and only work on the PTZ-S310 / PTZ-S330 SKUs — fill in the username/password fields if you need them.
4. VISCA-over-IP supports multiple controllers per camera, so OpenAVC can co-exist with a hardware joystick or other control surface.

compatible_models.notes: Verified against AVer's VISCA Specification 3.3 (April 2025) and the PTZ310/330 HTTP CGI Commands document (June 2022). Both transports use the same camera IP. Reboot and Factory Reset require Basic auth on PTZ-S310/S330 SKUs; configure a username/password on those models.

drivers.name: Barco ClickShare CX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Wireless presentation Base Unit control via local REST API V2 (HTTPS, port 4003). System status, standby / wake / reboot, audio + video + wallpaper + CEC, paired-button readback. Covers CX-20 / CX-30 / CX-50, C-5 / C-10 / C-10A, CB-Core / CB-Pro.

help.overview: The ClickShare Base Unit exposes a local REST API on port 4003 (HTTPS). Use this driver to mirror runtime status (is anyone sharing?), force the Base Unit into / out of standby, reboot, and switch audio output / wallpaper / video mode under macro control. Typical room logic: when the room shutdown macro fires, send `standby`; when the room comes up, send `wakeup` (or rely on the Base Unit's auto-wake on first share).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Base Unit — its
   Ethernet MAC is on the bottom label. Leave port 4003 open between
   the OpenAVC server and the Base Unit.
2. In the Base Unit's web Configurator (https://<base-unit>), open
   Security → Pin Code / API and confirm the API is enabled. Default
   credentials are integrator / integrator. Change them and supply
   the new ones below.
3. (Recommended) Replace the self-signed HTTPS certificate with one
   trusted by the OpenAVC host, then flip "Verify SSL Certificate"
   on. The driver works either way; verifying is just defense in
   depth.
4. Click Save. The driver polls every 30 seconds by default — drop
   to 10 s if you need faster sharing-state updates (the Base Unit
   can handle it; ClickShare's own integrations poll more frequently).

compatible_models.notes: Same V2 REST API across the entire CX / C / CB family. Feature differences (number of paired buttons, dual video outputs on CX-50 Gen2, UVC pass-through on CX-30 Gen2 / CX-50 Gen2) are reported by the Base Unit at runtime in the `supportedOutputs`, `supportedModes`, `supportedPowerModes`, etc. arrays — the driver doesn't need to know the model. Older CSE / CSC ClickShare units use a different (legacy) API and are NOT covered.

drivers.name: Behringer X32 Digital Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Behringer X32 and X32 Compact digital mixing consoles via OSC. 32 input channels, 16 mix buses, 6 matrices, 8 DCAs, 8 aux inputs, 8 FX returns, main stereo and mono outputs. Also compatible with Midas M32.

help.overview: Controls a Behringer X32 or X32 Compact digital mixer over the network using the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol. Full console coverage including all 32 input channels, 16 mix buses, 6 matrices, 8 DCAs, 8 aux inputs, 8 FX returns, and main stereo/mono outputs.
help.setup:
1. Connect the X32 to the same network as the OpenAVC server. 2. On the X32, go to Setup > Network and note the IP address. 3. Enter the IP address in the device config. The default port is 10023. 4. The driver will automatically subscribe to feedback and start
   receiving fader/mute updates.

compatible_models.notes: Identical OSC protocol to X32.

drivers.name: Biamp Tesira TTP
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Biamp Tesira and TesiraFORTÉ DSPs over the Tesira Text Protocol on TCP port 23 (Telnet). Supports Mute, Level, Source Selector, Matrix Mixer (crosspoints), Auto Mixer, Router, Logic, AEC, Room Combiner, Audio Meter, Signal Present Meter, Tone Generator, Preset recall, and basic VoIP / Dialer surfaces. Subscribes to push updates instead of polling. Declare your Tesira blocks once in the device config — the driver expands per-block / per-channel state variables and commands automatically.

help.overview: Comprehensive Biamp Tesira / TesiraFORTÉ control over TTP (Telnet, port 23). The driver subscribes to per-block, per-channel state changes — UI bindings update in real-time without polling. Declare every Tesira block you want to monitor or control in the 'DSP Block List' field below; the driver expands one state variable per (block, attribute, channel) and surfaces typed commands named after each block.
help.setup:
STEP 1 — Enable network control on the DSP.
Open Tesira software, connect to the unit, and go to Tools → Device Maintenance → Network Settings. Tick 'Discovery Service' and 'Telnet' (both default OFF). Leave 'System Security' OFF too — this driver expects an unauthenticated Telnet session, which matches the standard deployment when the DSP is on a private AV VLAN. Apply.

STEP 2 — Find your Instance Tags.
Open the Tesira design (.tmf file) for this DSP. Each control block (Mute, Level, Source Selector, Mixer, AEC, Room Combiner, etc.) has a user-assigned 'Instance Tag' — right-click any block → Properties → top of the dialog. Tags are case-sensitive: 'Level1' and 'level1' are NOT the same. For multi-channel blocks (e.g. a 4-mic Mute), note how many channels are wired up — that's the channel count you'll declare below.

STEP 3 — Enter the device IP address above.

STEP 4 — Declare your blocks in the 'DSP Block List' field below.
Format: one block per line, whitespace-separated
    <INSTANCE_TAG> <TYPE> [CHANNELS|NxM]

Examples (typical conferencing room):
    Mute1     mute        1-4         # 4 mic mute channels
    Level1    level       1-4         # 4 mic level channels
    PgmMute   mute        1           # program-out mute
    PgmLvl    level       1           # program-out level
    PgmSrc    source_select           # source selector
    AEC1      aec         1-2         # 2-channel AEC
    Combiner1 room_combiner 1-4       # 4-wall combiner
    PgmMix    matrix_mixer 8x4        # 8 inputs × 4 outputs

Notes on the syntax:
    • CHANNELS can be '1', '1-4' (range), or '1,3,5' (list)
    • NxM for matrix_mixer is INPUTS × OUTPUTS (e.g. 8x4 = 8 inputs, 4 outputs)
    • If you omit CHANNELS, channel 1 is assumed
    • Lines starting with '#' or ';' are comments — keep them as a reference or delete them
    • The pre-filled textarea has a complete syntax guide

STEP 5 — Save.
Within seconds the device should show 'Connected'. Open Variables → Devices and you'll see one state variable per (block, attribute, channel) — e.g. 'Level1_level_3' for the third channel of the Level1 block. Bind those state keys to UI elements, or use the auto-named per-block commands (e.g. 'Level1: Set Level (dB)') in macros and panel buttons.

Troubleshooting:
    • 'Connection lost' loop on port 22 — that's SSH, not       supported. Use port 23 (Telnet).
    • Device shows Connected but no state variables —       check that Telnet is enabled in System Manager AND       that your Instance Tags match exactly (case       matters).
    • Some channels don't update — verify the channel       count in your block list matches the actual wired       channel count in the Tesira design.
    • Need a block type the driver doesn't handle? Use       the generic 'Send Raw TTP Command' / 'Set       Attribute' commands — anything Tesira's command       string calculator generates will work.

compatible_models.notes: Every Tesira / TesiraFORTÉ DSP that runs Tesira software shares the same TTP protocol. Driver covers the block types AV integrators commonly use for room control. Setup: in Tesira's System Manager → Network Settings, enable Discovery and Telnet (both default OFF). Leave System Security disabled for the no-credentials path used by this driver.

drivers.name: BirdDog NDI Encoder/Decoder
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders via REST API. Select NDI sources on decoders, monitor input/output status, reboot, and refresh source lists.

help.overview:
Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders — Mini, Flex, 4K HDMI, 4K SDI, Studio NDI, PLAY, Quad, and similar models.

For decoders: select which NDI source to display, cycle through available sources, and monitor the active source.

For encoders: monitor input status and NDI source name.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the device's IP address (find it via BirdDog Central or your network's DHCP table).
2. Default port is 8080.
3. No authentication is required.
4. For decoders, use 'select_source' with the full NDI source name (e.g., 'BIRDDOG-P200 (Camera)').
5. Use 'refresh_sources' to update the available source list.

drivers.name: BirdDog PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog PTZ cameras via REST API and VISCA. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets, exposure, white balance, tally, and NDI encode settings.

help.overview:
Controls any BirdDog PTZ camera — P100, P200, P240, P400, A200, A300, X1, MAKI, and newer models. Uses the built-in REST API for configuration and VISCA-over-UDP for real-time PTZ movement.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the camera's IP address (find it via the camera's on-screen display or BirdDog Central).
2. Default REST port is 8080, VISCA port is 52381.
3. No authentication is required.
4. Use 'recall_preset' and 'save_preset' with preset numbers (1-255 depending on model).

drivers.name: Blackmagic Videohub
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Blackmagic Design Videohub routers over the Videohub Ethernet Protocol (TCP 9990). Supports video output routing, monitoring output routing, input/output label editing, and output locking across the entire Videohub product line.

help.overview: Blackmagic Videohub is a family of SDI matrix routers used in broadcast, post-production, and live event facilities. This driver speaks the Videohub Ethernet Protocol, used by every Videohub server-class device since 2010. It exposes video routing, monitoring routing, lock state, and label editing as macro-callable commands.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Videohub to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the unit's IP address from the front panel (Smart Videohub) or from Blackmagic Videohub Setup.
3. The Videohub Ethernet Protocol on TCP 9990 is always enabled — no auth, no enable step.
4. Enter the IP address in the device config; leave port at 9990.
5. Outputs and inputs are 1-indexed in commands.
6. Routing 'output X to input Y' sends VIDEO OUTPUT ROUTING with the protocol's 0-indexed values.

compatible_models.notes: All current Videohub products share the v2.3 Ethernet Protocol. Pre-declared state variables cover the first 16 video ports + 4 monitoring outputs; routing on wider frames still works, additional ports surface as raw keys.

drivers.name: Christie Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Christie commercial projectors using the Christie Serial API on TCP 3002. Supports the M, J, HS, H, GS, G, and E series families and their derivatives. Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, test patterns, brightness/contrast, freeze, orientation, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls for status; the projector also reports model, firmware, and projector hours.

help.overview: Christie commercial projectors that speak the Christie Serial API (M Series, J Series, HS / H Series, GS / G Series, E Series, Roadie). Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, brightness, contrast, freeze, orientation, test patterns, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls every 30 seconds for status. For commands not exposed here, use Send Raw Command — the full command list is in the Christie Serial API Technical Reference for your projector series.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to your network. 2. On the projector menu, enable Ethernet and note the IP address. 3. The Christie Serial API listens on TCP 3002 by default and does
   not require authentication.
4. Set the projector's "Serial Mode" / "Serial API" to enabled if
   it is not already on. (M Series MENU > Configuration >
   Communications > Network Settings.)
5. The Input Select command takes a two-digit slot+input code
   (e.g. 12 = slot 1 input 2). The slot/input map is on the back
   panel of the projector.

compatible_models.notes: All series share the same (CODE) message format and the core power / shutter / input / image controls. Series-specific features (e.g. laser-light controls on HS, lens-shift codes on GS) are not exposed here; use send_command with the series' published command list when needed. Boxer / Inspire / 4KHS / Crimson use a newer JSON / Christie API and require a different driver — they are not covered here.

drivers.name: Cisco Webex Codec / Room Series (xAPI)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Cisco Webex video-conferencing endpoints (Codec Pro / Plus / EQ, Room Bar, Room Kit family, Room 55/70 family, Board Pro, Desk family) via the RoomOS xAPI over HTTPS. Standby, volume, mute, dial / hangup, DND, presentation, camera presets, on-screen messaging, reboot. Polling-based — HttpFeedback push deferred until the platform's inbound-listener primitive lands.

help.overview: Cisco Webex video-conferencing endpoints — the Codec Pro / Plus, Room Kit family, Room 55 / 70 series, Board Pro, and Desk Pro — all expose the same xAPI over HTTPS. This driver covers the controls an AV integrator actually wires to a touch panel: standby on / off, volume, mute, dial, hangup, do-not-disturb, presentation start / stop, camera presets, and on-screen messages. xConfiguration writes are intentionally NOT included — settings belong in the Cisco web UI at install time, not on a control surface where they can be changed by accident.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the codec. 2. In the codec's web UI (https://<codec-ip>) go to Users and create
   (or note) a local user with at least the "Integrator" role. The
   default "admin" user works too. This driver uses HTTP Basic auth —
   SSO / single-sign-on users will not work.
3. Confirm xAPI over HTTPS is enabled. In the web UI: Settings ->
   Configurations -> NetworkServices -> HTTP Mode. Default is
   HTTP+HTTPS, which is fine. (HTTP-only is also supported by toggling
   the Use HTTPS field on this device.)
4. Add the codec in OpenAVC: enter the IP, leave port 443 / HTTPS on,
   enter the username and password from step 2.
5. Polling refreshes system info, standby, audio, DND, presentation,
   and people-presence every 30 seconds. Adjust the Poll Interval if
   you want faster touch-panel feedback.

compatible_models.notes: All models share the same RoomOS xAPI surface; one driver covers the whole family. Verified against the xAPI documentation; no live-hardware verification yet. The xAPI has been stable across CE9 / RoomOS 10 / 11 / 12 — minor command additions but the core surface used here predates CE9.

drivers.name: Crestron Device (CIP discovery)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Discovery-only anchor for Crestron devices that answer the CIP probe on UDP 41794. Surfaces hostname, model, and firmware through discovery so vendor-specific Crestron drivers (DM NVX, future 3-Series / TSW) can claim the device as primary; otherwise the user gets a placeholder they can swap for a control driver later.

help.overview: Crestron 3-Series control systems, DIN-AP processors, TSW touch panels, and DM NVX endpoints answer a UDP probe on port 41794 with their hostname, model, and firmware version. This driver hosts that probe so the device shows up in OpenAVC's discovery panel — but it offers no control surface. To actually drive a Crestron device, install the matching specific driver (DM NVX for video endpoints; specific 3-Series / TSW drivers as they land in the catalog) and swap this entry for it on the device card.
help.setup:
1. Run a network scan from the discovery panel. 2. Crestron devices that answer the CIP probe surface with
   hostname / model / firmware populated.
3. If a more specific Crestron driver matches the device's OUI
   or vendor alias, that driver wins primary identification and
   this anchor demotes to an alternative on the dropdown.
4. If no specific driver matches, add this anchor — you'll get
   a placeholder device entry. Install / build the right
   Crestron control driver next, then swap it in.

models: Any Crestron device that answers the CIP probe (3-Series, MC4, CP3, RMC4, DIN-AP, TSW, DM NVX)
compatible_models.notes: Discovery-only entry. For control, use the matching specific Crestron driver (e.g. crestron_nvx for AV-over-IP endpoints).

drivers.name: Crestron DM NVX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Crestron DM NVX AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the REST API. Supports device status, video/audio source selection, stream routing, and AV I/O monitoring.

compatible_models.notes: Any Crestron DM NVX endpoint via REST API.

drivers.name: Epson Projector (ESC/VP21)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Epson business and installation projectors over ESC/VP21 wrapped in ESC/VP.net on TCP port 3629. Power, input, A/V mute, freeze, aspect ratio, color mode, lamp hours, and remote-key passthrough.

help.overview: ESC/VP21 is Epson's text-based projector control protocol. Over the network it runs inside ESC/VP.net on TCP port 3629 — the driver handles the binary handshake transparently. Most modern Epson projectors respond to PJLink as well, but the native ESC/VP21 surface gives access to color mode, aspect ratio, freeze, image-quality numerics, and the full virtual remote keypad — none of which PJLink covers.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network and assign a static IP.
2. In the projector's network menu, enable 'Network Standby' (or 'Standby Mode = Communication On' on older units) so the projector responds to network commands while powered off.
3. Confirm 'Control Communications' (some menus call this 'PJLink' or 'ESC/VP.net') is enabled.
4. Optional: if the projector has an ESC/VP.net password set in the web setup, this driver does not currently send a password — disable it for control use, or use the device's web UI for one-off setup.

models: EB-L Series (EB-L200X, EB-L520W, EB-L630U, EB-L1075U, EB-L1100U)
compatible_models.notes: ESC/VP21 is shared across Epson's business and installation projector lines. Per-model variation is in which input codes the projector actually accepts (e.g. older units have no HDBaseT input). The driver lets the user pick from the union of all common codes; unsupported codes return ERR on the projector, which the driver logs at debug.

drivers.name: ETC Eos Family Console
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls ETC Eos family lighting consoles (Apex, Ti, Gio, Ion Xe, Element 2, Nomad/Eos PC) via OSC. Fire cues, fire macros, recall snapshots and presets, fire palettes, set channel/group/submaster levels, send raw command-line strings, press hardkeys/softkeys. Status pushed by Eos: current/pending cue text, command line, Live/Blind state, active cue progress.

help.overview: Controls an ETC Eos family lighting console (Apex, Ti, Gio, Ion Xe, Element 2, Nomad, Eos PC) over OSC (Open Sound Control) via UDP. Fire cues, fire macros, recall snapshots and presets, fire palettes, set channel/group/submaster levels, send raw command-line strings, or press any hardkey/softkey. Eos pushes the current command line, active cue text, pending cue text, Live/Blind state, and active cue progress percentage automatically.
help.setup:
1. On the console: Setup > System > Show Control > OSC.
   Enable both OSC RX and OSC TX. Set OSC UDP RX to 8000 and OSC UDP
   TX to 8001 (or any pair you prefer, then mirror the values in
   this driver's config).
2. Set OSC TX IP to the OpenAVC server's IP address. Eos will send
   all /eos/out/... status to that address on the OSC TX port.
3. In OpenAVC: enter the console's IP address as Host. Leave Port
   at 8000 and Listen Port at 8001 unless you changed them on the
   console.
4. Hardkey names for the press_key command match the labels printed
   on the console face panel, in lowercase, with spaces replaced
   by underscores (e.g. "go", "stop", "go_to_cue", "live", "blind",
   "select_last", "clear_cmd_line"). The full list lives in the
   Eos Family Online Help under "OSC Key Names".

compatible_models.notes: All Eos-family consoles share the same OSC dictionary documented in the Eos Family Online Help. ColorSource AV exposes a subset of the same /eos OSC namespace.

drivers.name: Extron SIS Protocol
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Extron products via the SIS (Simple Instruction Set) protocol. Covers crosspoint matrix switchers (DXP, CrossPoint), presentation switchers (IN Series), scalers (DSC, DVS), distribution amplifiers, and DSP products. Works over TCP (port 23) or RS-232 (9600 8N1).

help.overview: Universal control for Extron products using the SIS protocol. Works with 200+ products including crosspoint matrix switchers, presentation switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and DSPs.
help.setup: 1. Connect the Extron device to the network or via RS-232 (9600 8N1). 2. For TCP control, set the device's IP address and use port 23 (default). 3. Extron recommends a 100ms delay between commands (pre-configured).

compatible_models.notes: Any Extron product implementing the SIS protocol (~200 products).

drivers.name: Art-Net DMX (Generic)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Sends DMX512 lighting data over Art-Net (UDP 6454) to any Art-Net-compatible node, gateway, fixture, or controller. Maintains a 512-byte channel buffer per universe in memory; commands set channels, blackout, or full-on; a periodic keep-alive re-broadcast keeps long-running shows alive on receivers that time out idle universes.

help.overview: Art-Net is the de-facto Ethernet protocol for DMX512 lighting. Controllers send ArtDmx packets to nodes (Art-Net to DMX gateways), or directly to network-native fixtures. The driver maintains a 512-channel buffer for each universe it controls and re-broadcasts on a 900 ms keep-alive cadence so the receiver doesn't drop the universe.
help.setup:
1. Set the target node's IP to a static address and put it on the same VLAN as the OpenAVC server. Art-Net traditionally uses the 2.x.x.x or 10.x.x.x range, but any reachable IP works.
2. Confirm the node's universe number — Art-Net calls it the Port-Address (0..32767). Most consoles and fixtures expose it as a Net + Subnet + Universe trio (7 + 4 + 4 bits); enter the combined 15-bit value here. Universe 0 is a common default.
3. To broadcast (one transmit reaches all nodes on the subnet), use the broadcast IP for your subnet. Unicast to a node's IP is preferred per the Art-Net 4 spec.
4. Run the ``set_channel`` or ``blackout`` command. The driver starts re-broadcasting automatically; no separate ``start`` is needed.

models: Art-Net Node / Gateway / Fixture (any conforming vendor)
compatible_models.notes: Art-Net is an open published standard maintained by Artistic Licence. This driver sends ArtDmx and works with any conforming Art-Net receiver. Brand-specific entries below name the major node / gateway / fixture vendors confirmed by their published product literature.

ETC's Response and Net3 gateway families translate Art-Net (and sACN) to physical DMX outputs. ETC's Eos console is also covered by the dedicated `etc_eos` OSC driver, which is the right choice when controlling cues directly rather than driving fixtures.
Pathway Pathport gateways translate Art-Net and sACN to DMX. Common in pro AV and theatrical installs.
Enttec ODE family converts Art-Net to DMX. ODE Mk3 also speaks sACN. The smaller-footprint DIN-ODE fits a DIN rail in install racks.
Elation E-Node series Art-Net / sACN to DMX gateways.
Chauvet Professional network nodes for entertainment lighting.
American DJ network DMX gateways.
Color Kinetics (Signify) architectural LED gateways. The controller side speaks Art-Net to drive Color Kinetics fixtures via PDS power/data supplies and Antumbra controllers.

MA Lighting Network Processing Units translate console output to Art-Net and sACN for downstream gateways. Useful for tracking backup or for sending Art-Net into an MA console for visualizer / pre-program workflows.
Madrix is primarily an Art-Net source for LED video pixel-mapping, but its Aura and Plexus hardware bridges accept Art-Net input and convert to DMX or playback stored shows.

drivers.name: Generic HTTP/REST Device
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Template driver for HTTP/REST-controlled devices. Supports JSON APIs with configurable authentication (none, basic, bearer, API key, digest) and optional HTTPS with self-signed certificate support.

help.overview: Template driver for controlling any device with an HTTP or REST API. Install this driver and add your own commands, state variables, and polling using the Driver Builder. Many modern AV devices expose REST APIs alongside traditional serial or TCP protocols.
help.setup:
1. Enter the device's IP address and HTTP port. 2. Configure authentication if the device requires it (basic, bearer,
   API key, or digest).
3. Enable HTTPS if the device uses TLS. Disable certificate verification
   for self-signed certs (common on AV equipment).
4. Use the Driver Builder to add commands and state variables for
   your specific device.

drivers.name: Generic VISCA-IP PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Generic Sony-specification VISCA-over-IP driver (UDP port 52381). Pan/tilt/zoom/focus, presets, auto-exposure, white balance, backlight, power. Covers Sony SRG/BRC, AVer, Marshall, Lumens and many other pro PTZ cameras that adopt Sony's wire format. PTZOptics uses a different framing on TCP/5678 -- prefer the dedicated `ptzoptics` driver for those.

help.overview: Generic Sony-specification VISCA-over-IP PTZ control on UDP port 52381. Supports the universal pan/tilt/zoom/focus + preset + AE/WB command surface. Where a brand-specific driver exists in the catalog, that driver covers more and is preferred.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and place it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. Enable VISCA over IP on the camera (often labeled 'VISCA over IP' or 'IP CONTROL' in the network menu). The default port 52381 should not need to change.
3. Confirm the camera is set to UDP — not TCP. Some cameras let you choose; this driver speaks UDP only.
4. Note: VISCA over IP supports up to 5 simultaneous controllers per camera, so multiple control surfaces (OpenAVC + a hardware joystick + a Bitfocus Companion page, etc.) can co-exist.

compatible_models.notes: Sony's VISCA-over-IP wire format is the de-facto cross-vendor standard for pro PTZ cameras. Brand-specific drivers expose more (vendor-specific image presets, preset-name strings, OSD/menu, lens controls) and should be preferred when available.

Older Sony EVI cameras that speak Sony-spec VISCA-IP but predate the BRC/SRG picture-profile / PRESET MODE / PTZ TRACE / tally surface. For SRG-X400/X402/201M2, SRG-X120/HD1M2, and BRC-X400/X401/H800/H900 use the dedicated `sony_visca` driver instead -- it adds picture profiles, R/B gain, color matrix, defog, PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally, IR correction, AF mode, AE speed, min/max shutter, high sensitivity, and OSD.

AVer's published 'VISCA over IP' protocol guide uses UDP 52381 with the Sony 8-byte header (verified against AVer's VISCA Specification 3.3). For the PTZ310 / PTZ330 family use the dedicated `aver_ptz` driver instead -- it adds AVer's HTTP CGI surface (image quality, SmartShoot, SmartFraming, RTMP, bulk status) on top of the VISCA-IP wire format. Other AVer cameras don't have a comparably documented HTTP CGI guide and continue here.
Marshall's CV-series broadcast PTZ cameras list VISCA over IP as a control method in their installation manuals.

drivers.name: PJLink Class 1 Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls any PJLink Class 1 compatible projector.

help.overview: Universal projector control via the PJLink Class 1 standard. Works with 100+ models from Epson, NEC, Panasonic, Sony, Christie, Hitachi, BenQ, Optoma, Canon, Barco, Fujifilm, and Vivitek. Where a brand has its own dedicated driver in the catalog (Panasonic PT, Sharp NEC, Sony VPL, Epson ES/VP, Barco Pulse), prefer that driver — it generally exposes more capability than PJLink's universal subset.
help.setup:
1. Enable network control on the projector (varies by manufacturer)
2. Assign a static IP address to the projector
3. If authentication is enabled, set the PJLink password
4. Default port is 4352 (PJLink standard)

compatible_models.notes: PJLink is a JBMIA cross-vendor standard. Any projector advertising PJLink Class 1 (or Class 2) support in its datasheet should work with this driver. Brand-specific drivers (when available) generally expose more — lamp diagnostics, vendor-specific picture modes, faster polling, extended status — and should be preferred over PJLink.

Panasonic commercial PT- series. Datasheets confirm Class 1 + 2. The dedicated `panasonic_pt` driver covers more (NTCONTROL Protocol 2 with md5 session auth, lamp/laser diagnostics) — prefer it when available for the same model.

models: Sharp XP Series (XP-P701U, XP-P621U, XP-X171Q, XP-V series)
compatible_models.notes: Combined Sharp NEC Display Solutions lineup (post-2020 merger). Sharp XP series and NEC PA/PX/PH/ME/M/NP series. JBMIA-registered for Sharp XP models. NaViSet Administrator is the vendor's own richer control software; PJLink is the open cross-vendor fallback. The dedicated `sharp_nec_projector` driver covers more (NEC native command set, lens/zoom/shift control).

Sony VPL data projectors. Configure via Web Advanced Menu → PJLINK. Up to 3 controllers can connect simultaneously. The dedicated `sony_vpl` driver (ADCP / SDAP) covers more (SHA-256 challenge-response auth, native lens controls).
JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Modern Epson commercial laser/lamp models. The dedicated `epson_escvp` driver covers more (ESC/VP command set, faster, brand-specific picture modes).
BenQ commercial install projectors with the network function enabled. Activated via the Network setting on the projector menu.

models: Professional J-Series (JEV, JSV, JNV, JWV, JTV, JCV, JPV)
compatible_models.notes: JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Optoma commercial / professional install projectors.
Christie commercial laser and lamp projectors. PJLink alongside Christie's native serial / IP API. Some models require enabling network IP control before PJLink will respond.
Barco F-series and Loop projectors. PJLink is a fallback to Barco's native Pulse REST API which exposes more capability.
Hitachi commercial projectors with the network/LAN module fitted. Not all Hitachi models include networking — check the datasheet.
Canon XEED commercial install projectors. Canon's product literature lists PJLink as a supported network control method.
JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Fujifilm folded-light-path ultra-short-throw commercial projectors.
Vivitek (Delta Electronics) commercial install projectors with the network function. Confirm PJLink in the model's datasheet.

drivers.name: Wake-on-LAN
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets to wake devices on the network. No persistent connection required.

help.overview: Sends Wake-on-LAN magic packets to power on devices remotely. Works with any Ethernet device that supports WoL (most PCs, NUCs, some displays, and media players).
help.setup:
1. Enable Wake-on-LAN in the target device's BIOS/UEFI settings
2. Enable WoL in the OS network adapter settings
3. Enter the target device's MAC address (e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF)
4. The broadcast address is usually 255.255.255.255 (default)

drivers.name: Kramer Protocol 3000
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Kramer products via Protocol 3000 over TCP (port 5000). Covers matrix switchers (VS series), scalers (VP series), distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems.

help.overview: Controls Kramer matrix switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems via Protocol 3000. Common in corporate AV, education, and houses of worship.
help.setup:
1. Connect the switcher to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the IP address via the front panel menu or Kramer Network. 3. Enter the IP address and port 5000 (default) in the device config. 4. Machine number defaults to 01. Change it if multiple Kramer units
   share the same port.

compatible_models.notes: Any Kramer product implementing Protocol 3000.

drivers.name: LG SICP Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls LG commercial displays via SICP over TCP (port 9761). Supports power, input, volume, mute, and screen mute. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.

help.overview: Controls LG commercial displays via the SICP protocol. Supports power, input selection, volume, mute, and screen mute. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.
help.setup: 1. Connect the LG display to the network. 2. Default control port is 9761. 3. Set the Display ID (01-99, or 00 for broadcast to all displays).

drivers.name: LG WebOS
drivers.author: Keaton Stacks
drivers.description: Controls LG WebOS TVs (2016+) via the SSAP WebSocket protocol.

help.overview: Controls LG WebOS televisions using the SSAP protocol over a secure WebSocket connection on port 3001.  Supports power, volume, input switching, and app launching.
help.setup: Enable 'LG Connect Apps' or network control in the TV's General settings. A pairing prompt will appear on the TV screen on first connect. If the prompt does not appear, use the 'Force Pair' command.

drivers.name: Lightware LW3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lightware switchers and matrix routers via Protocol #3 (LW3) over TCP port 6107. Covers UCX, Taurus UCX, MMX2, MMX, and MX2M products. Provides video and audio crosspoint switching, mute, lock, HDCP, output 5V, embedded- audio mute, EDID switching, analog audio level/mute/balance, and CEC command sending.

help.overview: Lightware LW3 is the unified ASCII control protocol used across Lightware's matrix switchers, extenders, and modular routers. Commands target a tree of nodes (e.g. /V1/MEDIA/VIDEO/XP) using GET, SET, and CALL operations. The driver exposes the most-used runtime control surface: video and audio routing, mute, HDCP, output power, EDID, analog audio level, and CEC.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Lightware device to the network via Ethernet. 2. Confirm the device's IP address using LDC (Lightware Device Controller)
   or the front-panel display.
3. In LDC's Network tab, ensure the LW3 service on port 6107 is enabled
   and that authentication (IPLogin) is OFF — this driver does not
   authenticate.
4. Enter the IP address and port 6107 in the device config. 5. Use input/output port numbers as integers (I3 → input=3, O2 → output=2).
   Setting input=0 disconnects an output.
6. Polled state covers I1..I4 and O1..O4. Larger devices respond to
   routing commands on any valid port number.

compatible_models.notes: Any Lightware product that implements LW3 (most products since 2012). Polled state covers ports I1..I4 and O1..O4 — adequate for UCX, Taurus, and MMX2; commands accept any port number for larger MX2M frames.

drivers.name: Lutron HomeWorks QS
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lutron HomeWorks QS Processors (HQP6-2, HQP7) over Telnet using the Lutron Integration Protocol (LIP). Supports zone level control (OUTPUT), keypad/phantom button presses and LED control (DEVICE), area occupancy queries (AREA), and shade group control (SHADEGRP). Use phantom keypad button presses to activate scenes.

help.overview: Lutron HomeWorks QS is a residential and small-commercial lighting, shade, and HVAC control system. The HomeWorks QS Processor exposes a Telnet integration protocol (LIP) on port 23 that lets external controllers raise/lower lights and shades, press phantom keypad buttons (which activate scenes programmed in the Lutron design software), and monitor occupancy.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the HomeWorks QS Processor's IP address (set a static
   reservation on the network).
2. In the HomeWorks QS Design software, on the Integration tab,
   assign Integration IDs to the outputs, devices (keypads), areas,
   and shade groups you want to control. Note them down — you'll
   reference them in macros and triggers.
3. Confirm a Telnet login exists for integration use. Defaults are
   "lutron" / "integration" but the integrator may have changed
   them in the design software. Enter the username and password
   in the device config below.
4. To activate a scene: program a phantom keypad in the design
   software, assign each button to a scene, then use the
   "Press Button" command with that keypad's Integration ID and
   the button's Component Number.
5. Zone (OUTPUT) levels are 0-100 percent. Fade and Delay times
   are optional and accept SS.ss, SS, MM:SS, or HH:MM:SS formats.

compatible_models.notes: HomeWorks QS Processor (HQP6-2 and HQP7). Other Lutron systems (RadioRA 3, Caseta SB Pro, Athena, QS Standalone) speak related but distinct protocol surfaces and are not covered by this driver.

drivers.name: Mersive Solstice Pod
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Mersive Solstice Pods (and Solstice Windows Software) over the OpenControl REST API. Boot users, clear posts, suspend and wake the display, reset the on-screen key, push bulletin or emergency banners, and monitor connected users and post counts.

help.overview:
Mersive Solstice is a wireless presentation system. Users share screens, video, and media from laptops, phones, and tablets to a Solstice Pod that drives the room display.

OpenAVC controls the Pod's runtime: clear posts, boot all users at end-of-meeting, sleep / wake the display, reset the on-screen connection key, and push bulletin or emergency banners. Live state includes connected users, active posts, bandwidth, and the current screen key.

Install-time configuration (network setup, calendar integration, splash-screen images) stays in the Solstice Dashboard. RS-232 pass-thru is exposed for chained-display control via a USB-to-serial adapter on the Pod.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the Pod has Solstice Enterprise Edition. The OpenControl API is gated to Enterprise hosts.
2. In the Solstice Dashboard, set an admin password (strongly recommended — without one, any device on the network can drive this Pod).
3. Enter the Pod's IP address and admin password here. Default port is 80 (HTTP). Tick Use HTTPS for port 443; Solstice ships with a self-signed certificate which the driver does not verify.
4. Mersive recommends polling no more than once every 10 seconds. The default interval is 30 s; the minimum is 10 s.

compatible_models.notes: Requires Solstice Enterprise Edition license — Standard Edition Pods do not expose the OpenControl API. Some commands are Pod-only (reboot, hardware variant, HDMI input force-off); Windows Software hosts ignore them. Power-management / suspend / wake are Pod-only.

drivers.name: Middle Atlantic RackLink PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Middle Atlantic / Legrand RackLink RLNK power distribution units (Select, Premium, Premium+) over the RackLink Control Protocol on TCP port 60000. Outlet and dry-contact control, sequencing, naming, EPO, and live voltage / current / temperature / wattage telemetry. Premium models push unsolicited status changes; Select models fall back to polling.

help.overview: RackLink is the Middle Atlantic (now Legrand AV) family of network-controlled rack PDUs commonly installed in commercial AV racks. The driver speaks the binary RackLink Control Protocol so macros can switch outlets on / off, cycle outlets to power-cycle frozen gear, sequence the rack up / down, and (on Premium / Premium+ units) read live telemetry.
help.setup:
1. Connect the PDU to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the PDU's IP from the RackLink front panel or web UI.
3. Log into the PDU's web UI as Administrator and set the passwords for Administrator, User, and Control Systems accounts. The control protocol is disabled until those passwords are set.
4. On Premium+ models, enable the control protocol under Device Settings → Network Services → Control Protocol, and enter a username for an admin account that has the control protocol enabled.
5. Enter the IP, port 60000, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC. Default Select / Premium credentials are user / password (whatever was set in step 3).

compatible_models.notes: All RackLink series share the Control Protocol on TCP 60000. Select models support outlet control, naming, sequencing, and dry contacts. Premium and Premium+ add per-system telemetry (voltage, current, wattage, temperature, surge state, occupancy), EPO, and pushed status updates.

drivers.name: Novastar H Series Video Wall Splicer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Novastar H series video wall splicers via UDP JSON commands. Covers layer operations, preset management, input switching, brightness, fade-to-black, freeze, volume, test patterns, screen color, OSD, and device management. Compatible with H2, H5, H9, H15, H20, and similar models using the H Series Control Protocol.

help.overview: Controls Novastar H series LED video wall splicers. These processors manage LED wall layouts, input routing, presets, and screen settings. Common in large-format LED installations including houses of worship, corporate lobbies, broadcast studios, and live event stages.
help.setup:
1. Connect the processor to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the processor's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 3. Enter the IP address and port 6000 (default) in the device config. 4. Device ID defaults to 0. If using multiple processors, set the
   device_id config field to match each unit's ID.
5. Screen ID defaults to 0. Set screen_id for multi-screen setups.

drivers.name: ONVIF Camera (discovery)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Discovery-only anchor for cameras and AV devices that answer the ONVIF WS-Discovery multicast probe. Surfaces manufacturer, hardware model, and ONVIF service URLs in scan results so vendor-specific camera drivers can claim the device as primary; otherwise the user gets a placeholder they can swap for a control driver later.

help.overview: ONVIF cameras advertise themselves on the local network via SOAP-over-UDP WS-Discovery (multicast group 239.255.255.250 port 3702). A scan listens for ProbeMatch responses and reads each camera's manufacturer + hardware fields from the scope URIs so the matcher can identify the device. Use this anchor when no vendor-specific driver is available; replace it with the vendor's control driver once one ships in the catalog.
help.setup:
1. Run a network scan from the discovery panel. 2. ONVIF cameras that answer the multicast Probe surface with
   manufacturer, hardware model, and ONVIF service URLs read from
   their scope URIs.
3. If a vendor-specific camera driver matches the device's
   manufacturer or OUI, that driver wins primary identification
   and this anchor demotes to an alternative.
4. If no specific driver matches, add this anchor — you'll get
   a placeholder device entry surfacing the camera's identity.
   Install / build the right control driver next and swap it in.

models: Any IP camera or AV device that answers ONVIF WS-Discovery with a NetworkVideoTransmitter scope (Axis, Hanwha, Hikvision, Bosch, Sony, Panasonic, AVer, Vaddio, PTZOptics, Lumens, Marshall, etc.)
compatible_models.notes: Discovery-only entry. Tested against the ONVIF Network Specification §7 scope URI format; firmware variations in the SOAP envelope are tolerated. For control, use the matching vendor-specific camera driver once it ships in the catalog.

drivers.name: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic AW-HE, AW-UE, and AW-UN series professional PTZ cameras via the documented HTTP CGI protocol (port 80). Covers power, pan/tilt drive and absolute positioning, zoom, focus (auto/manual), iris (auto/ manual), 100 presets, tally, wireless remote enable, and zoom-linked pan/tilt speed. Image-quality controls (gain, white balance, scene files, gamma) are install-time setup left to the camera's web UI.

help.overview: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN are professional PTZ cameras commonly used in broadcast, houses of worship, lecture capture, and corporate AV. The cameras are controlled over HTTP using a small CGI command set. This driver exposes the full pan/tilt/zoom/focus/iris/preset/tally surface needed for live room control. Image quality settings (color, gain, white balance, scene files) are configured in the camera's web UI.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the camera via its web UI (default credentials
   are typically admin / 12345 — change them).
2. Enter the camera's IP address below. Default port is 80. 3. If you've enabled HTTP authentication on the camera, set Auth Type
   to "basic" and enter the username and password.
4. Pan/tilt drive uses speed values 01..99 per axis (50 = stop, 50/50
   both stop). The home position is APC8000/8000.
5. Presets are numbered 1..100 in the UI; the protocol uses 0..99
   internally, but the driver exposes the 1..100 numbering.
6. Polling is set to 10 seconds by default. Keep this at or above 5 s
   — the cameras throttle aggressive polling and have a 130 ms minimum
   inter-command gap.

compatible_models.notes: All AW-HE / AW-UE / AW-UN PTZ models on firmware 4.x+. The AK-UB300 (box camera) is in the same protocol family but does not support most pan/tilt/zoom commands — it returns errors for unsupported operations which the driver simply ignores.

drivers.name: Panasonic PT-MZ / PT-RZ Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic PT-MZ (LCD) and PT-RZ (DLP) professional installation projectors via the NTCONTROL TCP protocol (Protocol 2). Power, input, shutter / AV mute, freeze, and operating-hours readout. Supports Panasonic's MD5 session-challenge authentication so the projector keeps its default Web Control admin password.

help.overview: Panasonic NTCONTROL (Protocol 2) is the TCP control channel shared across all Panasonic professional projectors. It runs on TCP 1024 by default with optional MD5 challenge-response authentication tied to the projector's Web Control admin account.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network and assign a static IP.
2. In the projector's main menu, set [Network] -> [Network Control] -> [Command Control] = ON. The default command port is 1024.
3. Open the projector's Web Control page in a browser. Set or change the Administrator-Authorized password (default username is ``admin1``, default password is ``panasonic``).
4. In OpenAVC, enter the projector's IP and the Web Control admin username and password. If you left the password blank in the projector's web UI (non-protected mode), leave the password field empty here too.

compatible_models.notes: Protocol 2 / NTCONTROL is the same on every Panasonic professional projector — the universal command surface (power, input select, shutter, freeze, operating hours) is consistent. Per-model variation is which physical inputs are present; the driver exposes the union and the projector returns ``ERR2`` for inputs it doesn't have, which the driver logs at debug.

drivers.name: Poly Studio (VideoOS)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Poly (HP) Studio X30, X50, X70, E70, and G7500 video collaboration bars via the public VideoOS REST API. Audio / video mute, volume, camera presets and direction nudges, hangup, reboot — everything needed to wire Poly bars into a touch panel.

help.overview: Poly VideoOS exposes a documented REST API on HTTPS 443 for control of audio mute, volume, privacy / video mute, camera control and presets, active call hangup, and system reboot. The driver uses session-cookie authentication — log in once with the device's admin credentials and the session is reused for the lifetime of the connection.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Poly bar to the network and assign a static IP.
2. From the bar's web UI (https://<ip>) sign in as Admin and confirm the API is enabled. The factory default password is the device's serial number on first boot — change it immediately to a site-specific password.
3. In OpenAVC, enter the bar's IP, the admin username (default ``admin``), and the password. Leave the port at 443.

compatible_models.notes: VideoOS REST API is identical across the X-series and G7500. Per-model differences (mic count, integrated cameras, bundled mic pods) don't change the command surface — they just gate which features actually do anything when invoked.

drivers.name: PTZOptics Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls PTZOptics PTZ cameras over the VISCA-over-IP protocol on TCP port 5678. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall / save / reset, tally light, image flip, auto-exposure mode, white balance mode, and backlight. Polled state covers pan / tilt / zoom / focus position, focus mode, AE mode, WB mode, backlight, and flip settings.

help.overview:
PTZOptics cameras are widely used in classrooms, houses of worship, and conference rooms. This driver speaks raw VISCA over TCP 5678 (no Sony VISCA-over-IP header), which is what PTZOptics cameras actually expose — UDP 1259 also works but TCP gives reliable delivery for absolute-position commands.

VISCA is request/response only. The driver polls the camera every few seconds for pan / tilt / zoom / focus position and exposure / WB state. Joystick-style movement uses pt_up / pt_down / etc. with pt_stop to halt; absolute moves use pt_absolute with explicit pan and tilt positions.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera's IP via the OSD menu, the PTZOptics utility, or your router's DHCP table.
2. Confirm VISCA-over-IP is enabled in the camera's web UI (Settings → Network or Settings → VISCA). Most cameras ship with it on by default.
3. Enter the IP in OpenAVC. Port 5678 is fixed.
4. After connecting, pan_position / tilt_position / zoom_position will populate automatically.
5. Save up to 128 presets (numbered 0–127). 'set preset speed' applies to subsequent recalls.

compatible_models.notes: All PTZOptics cameras share the same VISCA-over-IP command set on TCP 5678. Older models may not support every command (the camera ignores unknown ones). 12X-USB needs PTZOptics' IP/serial bridge for network control.

drivers.name: QSC Q-SYS QRC
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls QSC Q-SYS Cores via QRC (Q-SYS Remote Control) — JSON-RPC 2.0 over TCP port 1710. QRC is QSC's modern control protocol; ECP (port 1702) is legacy. Supports Named Controls, Component gain/mute, Mixer (per-input, per-output, crosspoint), Audio Router, Snapshot recall / save, Loop Player, and PA Router page submission. Uses Change Groups with auto-poll for push-style state updates instead of polling. Declare your Q-SYS blocks once in the device config — the driver expands per-block state variables and commands automatically.

help.overview: Comprehensive QSC Q-SYS control over QRC (JSON-RPC 2.0 on TCP 1710). The driver subscribes to every declared block via a Change Group with auto-poll — UI bindings update in real-time without polling. Declare every Q-SYS block you want to monitor or control in the 'Q-SYS Block List' field below; the driver expands one state variable per typed control and surfaces typed commands named after each block.
help.setup:
STEP 1 — Make sure QRC is reachable.
QRC is enabled by default on Q-SYS Cores running a design in Run mode. The default port is 1710. If your Core has admin authentication enabled (Users → Administrator), enter Username and Password below; otherwise leave them blank.

STEP 2 — Find your Code Names.
Open the Q-SYS design (.qsys file) for this Core in Q-SYS Designer. Each block (Gain, Mute, Mixer, Router, Snapshot Bank, Loop Player, etc.) has a Code Name on its Properties pane — that's the name QRC uses to address it. Right-click any block → Properties → 'Code Name'. Code names are case-sensitive: 'PgmGain' and 'pgmgain' are NOT the same.

Named Controls live in the Named Controls pane (Tools → Show Named Controls). The 'Name' column is what you declare here.

STEP 3 — Enter the Core's IP address above.

STEP 4 — Declare your blocks in the 'Q-SYS Block List' field below.
Format: one block per line, whitespace-separated
    <CODE_NAME> <TYPE> [SPEC]

Examples (typical conferencing room):
    PgmGain     gain                # program gain block
    RoomMute    mute                # whole-room mute
    PgmRouter   router    4         # 4-output source router
    RoomScenes  snapshot  8         # 8-snapshot bank
    BgmLoop     loop_player         # background-music loop
    Volume      named_control number   # volume Named Control
    Mute        named_control boolean  # mute Named Control
    DoorBell    named_control trigger  # trigger button
    PgmMix      mixer     8x4       # 8 inputs x 4 outputs
    LobbyZone   pa_zone             # PA Router zone

Notes on the syntax:
    • SPEC is type-dependent — 'NxM' for mixers, the output count for routers, the snapshot count for snapshot banks, the value type for named_control.
    • named_control type can be number / boolean / string / trigger. Default: number.
    • Lines starting with '#' or ';' are comments.
    • The pre-filled textarea has a complete syntax guide.

STEP 5 — Save.
Within seconds the device should show 'Connected'. The Core's status (Active / Idle / Standby), platform model, design name, and design code populate core_state, core_platform, etc. automatically. Open Variables → Devices and you'll see one state variable per typed control on each declared block — e.g. 'PgmGain_gain' (dB), 'PgmGain_mute' (boolean), 'PgmMix_xpoint_gain_3_2' (dB). Bind those state keys to UI elements, or use the auto-named per-block commands ('PgmGain: Set Gain (dB)') in macros and panel buttons.

Troubleshooting:
    • 'Connection refused' on port 1710 — verify the Core is in Run mode and that QRC isn't blocked by a VLAN ACL.
    • 'Logon required' errors — set Username and Password above to match a user defined under Q-SYS Administrator.
    • Some controls don't appear — check that the Code Names match exactly (case matters), and that the block exists in the currently-running design.
    • Need a block type the driver doesn't handle? Use 'set_component_control' or 'send_raw_jsonrpc' — anything QRC supports will work.

compatible_models.notes: Every Q-SYS Core that runs Q-SYS Designer software supports QRC. The driver speaks QRC (TCP 1710), not the legacy ECP (TCP 1702) — make sure the Core's Q-SYS firmware supports QRC (any version since Q-SYS 5.x). Setup: open your design in Q-SYS Designer, find the Code Names of the Components, Named Controls, Mixers, Routers, and Snapshots you want to control, then declare them in the block list below.

drivers.name: Samsung MDC Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Samsung commercial displays via the MDC (Multiple Display Control) binary protocol over TCP.

help.overview: Controls Samsung commercial displays using the MDC binary protocol. Covers Smart Signage, The Wall, LED, and SMART Signage Platform series.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display to the network
2. Enable MDC protocol in the display's network settings
3. Default port is 1515
4. Set the Display ID to match the display's configuration (default 1)

drivers.name: Sharp NEC Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp NEC projectors via the NEC binary control protocol over TCP. Compatible with P, PA, PE, PV, PX, ME, and M series projectors.

help.overview: Full-featured Sharp NEC projector control using the proprietary binary protocol on TCP port 7142. Power, input selection, picture/sound/OSD mute, freeze, shutter, volume, brightness, contrast, sharpness, aspect ratio, eco mode, lens control (zoom/focus/shift), lens memory presets, lamp/laser hours, filter hours, and detailed error status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network
2. Enable LAN control in the projector's network settings
3. Assign a static IP address to the projector
4. Default control port is 7142
5. This driver can coexist with PJLink (port 4352)
6. Set Standby Mode to 'Network Standby' or 'Sleep' to allow power-on via network
7. Input terminal codes vary by model — unsupported inputs are rejected gracefully

compatible_models.notes: Verified on hardware.
Per NEC protocol manual. Specific models like NP-P506QL fall under P series.

drivers.name: Shure Networked Devices
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Shure networked audio devices over TCP (port 2202). Covers MXA910/920/710 ceiling microphone arrays, ANI interfaces, P300 IntelliMix processor, and SCM820 automixer.

drivers.name: Philips Hue Bridge
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Philips Hue lights, rooms, zones, and scenes via the local REST API V1 on a Hue Bridge (HTTP, port 80). Recall scenes, on/off whole rooms, set brightness / color / color-temperature on groups or individual lights. Polling-based — the V1 API does not push.

help.overview: Philips Hue is the most widely deployed residential and small-commercial smart-lighting platform. The bridge sits on the LAN and bridges Zigbee bulbs / fixtures to a local REST API. AV integrators commonly use it for accent lighting in boardrooms, hospitality spaces, and houses of worship — recall a "Presentation" scene when the projector turns on, fade up "Q&A" lighting when the session ends.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Hue Bridge in your
   router. Default discovery is via mDNS (_hue._tcp) or the Signify
   cloud at https://discovery.meethue.com.
2. Press the round link button on top of the bridge. 3. Within 30 seconds, run the "Create User (Pair)" command from this
   device's Commands tab. The response will contain a username string
   like "abc123XYZ...". Copy that into the App Key field below.
4. Find the IDs of your lights, groups (rooms / zones), and scenes.
   The easiest way is to run the "Query All Lights", "Query All
   Groups", or "Query All Scenes" commands and read the IDs from the
   response. Light and group IDs are short numeric strings ("1", "2",
   "10"). Scene IDs are longer alphanumeric strings ("AB-cdef-12gh").
5. Use the light_* / group_* / recall_scene commands with those IDs.
   Group ID 0 is the special "all lights" group.
6. Polling is set to 30 seconds by default and only refreshes bridge
   metadata. Light / group state is not mirrored — read it on demand
   via the query_* commands.

compatible_models.notes: Both bridge generations expose the V1 REST API on port 80. The V2 bridge (square, BSB002) is the current production model and also supports the V2 / CLIP V2 API over HTTPS — this driver targets V1 only. The V1 bridge (round, BSB001) is end-of-life for new firmware but still functional.

drivers.name: Sonos Speaker
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sonos speakers via the local UPnP API. Play/pause, volume, mute, track info, and transport control.

help.overview: Controls any Sonos speaker on the local network via UPnP. Works with all Sonos models including One, Five, Beam, Arc, Era, Move, Roam, Port, Amp, and legacy Play/Connect models. No cloud account or API key required.
help.setup:
1. Ensure the Sonos speaker is on the same network
2. Enter the speaker's IP address (find it in the Sonos app under Settings > System > About)
3. Default port is 1400 (do not change)
4. UPnP control must be enabled on the speaker (on by default)

compatible_models.notes: UPnP API stable across all Sonos models.

drivers.name: Sony Bravia Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony Bravia TVs and professional displays via the JSON-RPC REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Power, input, volume, mute, navigation, media transport, app launch. Covers Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia models.

help.overview: Controls Sony Bravia displays using the built-in REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Works with Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia series from ~2013 onwards (W, X, Z, A, XR models).
help.setup:
1. Connect the TV to the network.
2. On the TV, go to Settings > Network > Home Network Setup > IP Control.
3. Set Authentication to 'Normal and Pre-Shared Key'.
4. Set a Pre-Shared Key (e.g., '1234').
5. Set Simple IP Control to 'On' (enables power-on over network).
6. Enter the TV's IP address and PSK in the driver config.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on production hardware.

drivers.name: Sony VISCA-IP PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Dedicated Sony SRG / BRC / EVI VISCA-over-IP driver (UDP port 52381). Adds Sony picture profiles, R/B gain, color matrix, defog, visibility enhancer, low-light, chroma suppress, PRESET MODE + PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, IR correction, ICR, AF mode, AE speed, min/max shutter, high sensitivity, and OSD on/off — on top of the standard PTZ + AE/WB command set.

help.overview: Sony PTZ camera control over VISCA-IP (UDP 52381). Includes Sony's own picture profiles, color matrix, PRESET MODE / PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, OSD, AF mode, AE speed, IR correction, ICR, and shutter limits.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and put it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. Enable VISCA over IP in the camera's network menu. The default port 52381 should not need to change.
3. Confirm the camera is set to UDP — not TCP. Sony BRC/SRG cameras default to UDP; this driver speaks UDP only.
4. VISCA over IP supports up to 5 simultaneous controllers per camera, so OpenAVC can co-exist with hardware joysticks or other control surfaces.
5. Picture-profile / color-matrix / defog / PRESET MODE commands only take effect on the BRC-X400/X401 — on smaller SRG models the camera silently rejects them.
